confirmed.description: Keshavrao's wrist manacles have no chain between them. His arms are flung more than a full span apart: Nagoji grips his left wrist cuff while his right cuff is out at the far right edge, free. That breaks the chapter's fixed rig (wrist manacles joined by a short chain about a forearm long) and the bible row for chapter 3, and it undercuts the later beats (9.1, 9.3, 8.3 inset) that depend on his wrist chain.
confirmed.evidence: Render page-03 panel 3 (roughly x 1000-1500, y 1150-1470 at full res): Keshavrao's right cuff is near the right border and his left cuff is in Nagoji's bandaged grip near centre, with no links between them. The unlettered frame page-03-panel-03-v05.png shows the same thing at full size.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed on page 3, panel 3. I zoomed into the r6 render at about x 316-1525, y 1150-1470 at full resolution. Keshavrao's arms are flung out to a full wingspan. His left wrist cuff is at the far right of the panel, against the barrel, and no chain is attached to it. His right cuff sits just below Nagoji's bandaged fist, near the centre. The two cuffs are about 570 px apart at 300 DPI, roughly 1.9 in printed and three times his forearm length. No links run between them, and none could run behind his body over that distance. The only chain on his right cuff runs left to Nagoji: Nagoji's collar chain and the loop from Nagoji's lower cuff meet there. The other chain in his area comes from his collar. The panel has no lettering, so nothing covers a chain.

Nothing allows this. Script 1.1 fixes one set of irons for the whole chapter, with wrist manacles joined by a short slack chain about a forearm long. Panel 3.3 itself mentions Keshavrao's cuffs. The other panels keep the rig: page 2 panel 3, and page 9 panels 1, 2 and 3, where the short chain between his wrists is plainly drawn. 9.3 even depends on that chain catching on the rope.

One part of the claim is wrong. The CONTINUITY.md chapter 3 row with the forearm-long chain is Nagoji's. Keshavrao's own bible entry (line 72) does not list his irons. The script's chapter-wide rig still covers him, so the finding stands.

The error is easy to see at print size. The chain-free cuff on his outflung arm is a clear shape at the panel's right edge, in a chapter about chains. It is still a localized prop and continuity error, not a matter of identity, lettering or a missing beat. That makes it major, not a blocker.

confirmed.description: The setting and water level change on the same page. In 5.2 and 5.3 the hold is crowded with chained prisoners sitting in waist- to chest-deep water. In 5.4 and 5.5 Nagoji and Keshavrao stand alone in a cavernous, empty barrel hall with the water only at their ankles. On page 4 (4.5) it was already waist-deep, and on page 6 (6.2) it is thigh-deep again.
confirmed.evidence: Render page-05: in panel 3 the prisoners around Nagoji are submerged to the chest. In panel 5 the water splashes at shin and ankle height around both men's ankle cuffs, and there are no pens and no other prisoners anywhere in the wide frame.

verdict.reason: Confirmed after zooming into page 5. In panel 5.3, Nagoji is standing and the waterline cuts across his upper thighs and hips. The seated prisoners around him are submerged to the waist or chest. In 5.4 the frame stops at the knees and shows no water there, which is already doubtful. In 5.5 the water only splashes around the ankle cuffs. Both men stand in what looks like a different room: a long, empty hall of pillars and barrels running off into blue distance, with no pens, no plank shelves and no other prisoners. Page 4, panel 5 sets the water waist-deep ("We will drown down here"), and page 6, panel 2 has it thigh-to-hip deep again, with Nagoji saying "we may drown". So 5.5 is the only panel that drains the hold and loses the pen setting, and it breaks continuity in the middle of the drowning threat. The script supports the art having no water depth or setting like this: 5.4 has their heels "braced against the plank of the pen", and 5.5 sends the chain "sliding away into the water between them", which assumes the same flooded pen. The cast overrides list only named characters (5.2 lists none, yet prisoners are drawn), so leaving out anonymous prisoners is not a script requirement on its own. The water level and the change of room are still clearly visible at print size. The problem is limited to one panel: identity, irons and the story beat are correct. That makes it major, not a blocker. Fix: redraw 5.5 inside the same crowded pen, with the water at least thigh-deep, as in 5.3 and 6.2.

confirmed.description: The props on page 2 don't match: this is the musket the script says to 'plant hard'. In 2.1 the hatch ladder is a steep, narrow ladder next to a post, and the musket has a large brass buttplate. In 2.4 the ladder has become a broad staircase with handrails, and the musket is a different gun: lighter studded stock, no brass buttplate, iron barrel bands.
confirmed.evidence: Render page-02 panel 1: a narrow ladder at the right edge, and the musket's brass buttplate in the foreground. Panel 4: a wide staircase with rails at the right, and the musket butt at the left with no brass plate.

verdict.reason: The differences are real, but they are polish-level, not major. Zoomed crops of page 2 show this. Musket: in 2.1 the butt is shown end-on with a large gold brass buttplate, plus a brass band near the muzzle and a plain lock. In 2.4 the butt is seen in profile with a pale steel rim, dark iron barrel bands and an engraved lockplate. The trigger guard is still gold in 2.4, so the lighting shows brass, and the steel rim is a real change of metal. The "studded" look of the stock is only water droplets. Ladder: 2.1 has a steep open-tread ladder beside the big post with the iron ring. 2.4 has a less steep, wider stair with plank stringers on both sides (not real handrails), water running down it and open sky above. Why it is not major: at print size (the page is about 6.1 x 9.25 in) the 2.4 musket still reads as the same weapon. It is the same brown walnut flintlock with a gold trigger guard, lying against a beam by the ladder foot, as the script says, and the brass buttplate cannot show end-on in a side view. The stair is a small background element at the far right of a narrow strip and reads as the same hatch way up toward grey light. No beat, identity or lettering is affected. The ladder is also loose across the whole chapter: page 6 draws it as a rope-and-rung ladder. So the 2.4 stair is one part of a chapter-wide ladder drift, not a local error on page 2. Fix in polish: give the 2.4 butt a brass edge and brass bands, and draw the ladder as the steep, narrow ladder from 2.1 (that also fits the page 6 caption about the ladder feeling narrow). Crops are in /tmp/claude-501/rf_ch3p2/.

confirmed.description: The guard's two balloons are ambiguous to read in order. Placement is also poor: the huge second balloon on the left is only slightly lower than the first one on the right, it covers the guard's torso and musket arm, it presses against the left panel border, and its last line is a single orphaned word ('over.').
confirmed.evidence: Page 1, panel 1.4: 'Quiet down there. No shouting. No prayers.' at x600-1000, y1273-1360; 'If any of you break your chains... throw you / over.' at x108-555, y1330-1495, touching the left border at x~110 and covering the guard's chest and musket hand.

verdict.reason:
I measured page 1, panel 1.4 at full resolution (1838x2775). The panel has real lettering faults, but they are minor polish, not major. Part of the reported problem is wrong.

1. Reading order is mostly clear, not ambiguous. The "Quiet down there" balloon on the right runs from y1765 to y1885. The "If any of you..." balloon on the left starts lower, at y1846. The right balloon's single text line (y1809-1840) ends more than 60 px (about 5 mm in print) above the first line of the left text (y1904). A reader will most likely read the higher balloon first, which matches the script order. The large left balloon does pull the eye a little.

2. The claim that the balloon covers the musket hand is wrong. The guard's hand, the musket lock and the stock sit just above the left balloon's top edge (around x580, y1810) and are fully visible. So are his face, the morion and the arm reaching to the hatch frame. The balloon covers only his lower left torso and jerkin, which do not carry the beat.

3. Two faults are real but minor:
   - The left balloon's outline touches the left panel border. Its white fill starts at x153 and its black outline merges with the border line at about x148-150 (around y1900-2040).
   - The last line is a single orphaned word, "over.", which a re-break would fix.

Both speaker tails point to the guard, and all the text is legible and matches the script. A small redraw would cover the fixes:
   - re-break the text to remove the orphan
   - pull the balloon in off the border
   - optionally drop it slightly lower so the reading order is beyond doubt

confirmed.description: The two Nagoji balloons are jammed into the top-left corner and onto the bottom border, sandwiching his small face between them. The first balloon also covers the left third of the shot, where the other men copy his grip on the beam.
confirmed.evidence: Page 3, panel 3.2: 'Hold to the beams! Hook your arms over the wood.' at x228-535, y570-695, with its outline running into the top and left panel borders; 'Do not let the chain drag you.' at x338-632, y735-822, with its bottom on the panel's bottom border. Nagoji's face is squeezed at about x570-640, y660-730 between the two balloons.

verdict.reason: I zoomed into page 3, panel 3.2 (original pixels x300-1540, y770-1160). Only a small part of the report holds up. The "major" level does not. Nagoji's face is not squeezed or hidden. His whole face, including the moustache, earring and open shouting mouth, sits clear between the two balloon tails, and both tails point cleanly at him. The key action is also all visible: both forearms hooked over the beam, cuffs and wrist chain on the wood. On the right, three men clearly copy the grip, so the script's "two or three men nearest him copy the grip" is met. The first balloon does hide the raised hands of the two background men at far left, but they are not needed for the beat. Reading order is clear: top-left first, then lower-centre. What is real is a lettering tangent. The first balloon's outline merges into the top and left panel borders, and the second balloon's flat bottom sits on the bottom border. At print size the balloons will look glued to the frame instead of floating or clearly breaking it. The second balloon also covers Nagoji's neck and chest, so the slack collar chain the script asks for is not seen. Both are polish problems. Fix: nudge both balloons about 15-25 px inward from the borders.

confirmed.description: In the three-balloon exchange, Keshavrao's follow-up question sits higher than Nagoji's off-panel answer. The natural zigzag reads 'Move where?' then 'And if there is no such thing?' and only then 'Towards air...', which scrambles the dialogue. The last balloon's tail tip also lands on Keshavrao's eye, and the balloon overlaps the right side of his head.
confirmed.evidence: Page 3, panel 3.5: 'Move where?' at y1505-1590; 'And if there is no such thing?' at x895-1085, y1560-1690, with its tail ending on his eye at about (840,1688); 'Towards air. Towards anything that floats.' at x275-628, y1610-1735.

verdict.reason: The problem is real; I confirmed it on a crop of page 3, panel 3.5 at full resolution. In the original pixels, 'Move where?' sits highest (top at about y=60 in the crop), and its tail points down and right toward Keshavrao, which pulls the eye to the right. 'And if there is no such thing?' sits on the right with its top at about y=135. Nagoji's off-panel line 'Towards air. Towards anything that floats.' sits on the left with its top at about y=200. So the right balloon is about 65 px (about 5 mm at 300 DPI) higher than Nagoji's answer, and the first tail leads straight to it. Readers following the usual 'higher first' path would read Move where? / And if there is no such thing? / Towards air, instead of the script's order (KESHAVRAO, NAGOJI off, KESHAVRAO). The words are clear enough that a reader can work out the right order, so this is not unreadable or a missing beat, but the order on the page is wrong. The tail of 'And if...' also ends right on Keshavrao's left eye (viewer's right), and the balloon's left edge covers the hair at his right temple above the ear. That is a smaller, polish-level flaw. The fix is to move 'And if there is no such thing?' below Nagoji's balloon (for example lower right, beside his cheek or jaw). It should not stack higher than 'Towards air', and its tail should end at his mouth or jaw, not his eye. Severity: major, because it is a localized lettering placement error that scrambles the reading order but needs no redraw of the art.

confirmed.description: Ragged page grid. The five panels have three different left edges and four different right edges, and gutters vary from about 5 px to 22 px. The bottom tier overhangs the tiers above on both sides, so the page does not read as one coherent grid like Chapter 1.
confirmed.evidence: Measured extents (display px): 6.1 and 6.2 at x142-1182; 6.3 at x173-1151; 6.4 at x107-660; 6.5 at x682-1200. The gutter between 6.3 and the bottom tier is about 6 px; between 6.4 and 6.5 it is about 22 px.

verdict.reason: The claim holds, but I rate it minor, not major. I measured page-06.png at full resolution (1838 px wide, 300 DPI). Every other page in the chapter uses one live area, x148 to 1688, with a 6 px gutter when a tier splits in two (split at x915/921 on pages 1, 2, 4, 5 and 7). Page 6 breaks from that. Tiers 6.1 and 6.2 sit at x197 to 1640, inset about 49 px on each side. Tier 6.3 sits at x240 to 1597, inset about 92 px. In the bottom tier, 6.4 runs x148 to 915, which is the full left margin, so it sticks out about 49 px past the tiers above. 6.5 runs x946 to 1664, short of the right margin by 24 px. The gutter between 6.4 and 6.5 is 30 px, five times the chapter standard. The vertical gutters are a normal 5 to 6 px. So there are three left edges and four right edges, as the reviewer said. Each panel is centred in its standard slot but shrunk to keep its own shape instead of being cropped to fill the slot. The page-6 script has no layout note that calls for staggered tiers. Page 3 also uses an inset column, but it is symmetric and consistent. The offsets are 2 to 8 mm in print, so they are visible and the page looks unfinished next to the rest of the chapter. Still, reading order, lettering and every story beat are intact. The fix is a relayout that crops the art to fill the standard slots, with no redraw, so this is polish rather than a clearly wrong, localized error.

confirmed.description: The dialogue is inverted and the reading path is muddled. Nagoji's reply 'Quickly.' sits on the left, where it is read first. Keshavrao's prompt 'Others.' sits to the right, against the top border, and its long thin tail ends at a lantern, well short of Keshavrao. The two captions are interleaved between and below the balloons. The script asks for both balloons at the left, at the start of the move.
confirmed.evidence: Page 6, panel 6.1: 'Quickly.' at x390-515, y318-400; 'Others.' at x780-900, y262-340, with its tail tip at about (700,315) while Keshavrao's head is at about (570,320); 'Liberty was a generous word.' at x578-853, y360-420; 'Yet slack iron...' at x765-1178, y435-528.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 6, panel 6.1, after zooming in. Nagoji's "Quickly." is the leftmost balloon, at about x390-515, y318-400 in the 1325-wide view, and its tail goes to Nagoji. Keshavrao's "Others." sits right of centre, at about x780-900, y262-340, above the three prisoners still chained. The two balloons overlap in height (y318-340), so they read as one row and the left one comes first. Readers will most likely meet Nagoji's reply before Keshavrao's prompt. At best the order is unclear. That flips the beat: in the script Keshavrao proposes freeing the others and Nagoji agrees. The tail of "Others." is long and thin and stops beside the lantern at about x700, well short of Keshavrao's head at about x570. It aims roughly toward him, so the speaker can still be worked out. But because the balloon sits over the right-hand prisoners, one of them could be taken as the speaker. Both captions sit between and below the balloons, so the reading path zigzags: Quickly., then up-right to Others., then back down-left to "Liberty...", then down-right to "Yet slack iron...". The script says plainly: "Letter the two balloons at the left, at the start of the move." The lettering ignores this. Nothing in the bible or script allows it. Every word is legible and the speakers can be identified, so this is not a blocker. It is a localized placement error that inverts the dialogue order and goes against a direct script instruction, so major is the right severity. Fix: move both balloons to the left, Others. first with its tail to Keshavrao, then Quickly. below or to the right of it with its tail to Nagoji, and put the two captions after them.

confirmed.description: The two insets along the bottom edge have no keyline or gutter. They butt straight onto the main image, and the 'Wait to free him...' caption rests directly on the top edge of the hatch inset. The insets therefore read as part of the deck scene, with the hatch apparently next to the rail, rather than as the flashes Nagoji takes in. The 9.1 inset does have a black keyline, so the two pages are also inconsistent.
confirmed.evidence: Page 8, panel 8.3: the boundary at y~1370 between the main image and the insets (hatch hands at x121-662, spar at x662-1205) is a raw image seam with no border. The caption box (x121-528, y1278-1370) ends exactly on that seam. Zoomed crop confirms no frame line.

verdict.reason: The missing keyline is real, but it is polish, not a major problem. I measured page 8 at full resolution (1838x2775). Real panel borders are 3 px of pure black (luminance 0) with a cream gutter, for example rows y2095-2097 and y2103-2105 at the bottom of panel 8.3. The seam between the 8.3 main image and the two insets, around y1899-1900, is only a 1-2 px darker band: row mean 26-34, row maximum 56-117, so not black and not a border. There is no gutter. The vertical join between the hatch inset and the spar inset (x~917) has no line at all, just a slight darkening. The 'Wait to free him...' caption box ends on that seam. The 9.1 inset on page 9 does have a black keyline, so the two pages are inconsistent. Nothing in the script or CONTINUITY.md asks for or excuses borderless insets. Why not major: at page size the bottom strip still reads clearly as two separate images. The jump from the side-on deck and rail to a top-down hatch and an open-water spar is abrupt, so the beat (Keshavrao's manacled hands on the hatch rim, then the shattered spar) gets across. No action is hidden and no attribution is wrong. The caption box's own black border even sits along part of the seam on the left. The effect is an unfinished-looking composite and a style mismatch with page 9. The fix is to add the same keyline and thin gutter as 9.1 around the two insets, and between them, in page 8, panel 8.3. No redraw is needed.

confirmed.description: Balloon reading order flips the exchange. Keshavrao's follow-up, "And if there is no such thing?", sits higher than Nagoji's off-panel answer, "Towards air. Towards anything that floats.", and the two balloons overlap vertically. A top-first reader gets the follow-up before the answer.
confirmed.evidence: "Move where?" is top centre (y about 1510). "And if there is no such thing?" is on the right (top y about 1565). "Towards air..." is on the left (top y about 1610). The script order is Keshavrao, Nagoji (off), Keshavrao.

verdict.reason: I could not refute this. I checked a crop of page 3, panel 5 at full resolution, and the reviewer's measurements are correct. Balloon tops in display coordinates are: "Move where?" at y 1508, "And if there is no such thing?" at y 1562 (right side), and "Towards air. Towards anything that floats." at y 1609 (left side, tail running off panel to the left). The right balloon is about 66 px higher than the left one at 300 DPI, roughly 5.6 mm in print, and its centre is higher by the same amount. It also overlaps "Move where?" vertically, so the two read as one tier. By the usual lettering rule (top to bottom, and a higher balloon on the right is read before a lower one on the left), a reader takes "Move where?", then "And if there is no such thing?", then "Towards air...". The script (3.5) orders it Keshavrao, Nagoji off-panel, Keshavrao, and neither the continuity bible nor the script allows this order. The follow-up "no such thing" comes before the "thing" is named, so the reader hits a non-sequitur and has to backtrack. The gap is not too small to matter: 5 to 6 mm at print size, with a clear diagonal eye path. The rating is major rather than blocker because both balloons are legible, correctly attributed and the beat is present. The fix is local: re-letter by moving the "Towards air" balloon up to sit clearly above the right balloon (or moving the right balloon down below it), with no redraw needed.

refuted.description: The tail on Nagoji's second balloon ("You have seen the dungeon... Tell me which death you prefer.") makes the line look like Keshavrao's. The balloon sits on Keshavrao's back in the foreground, and its tail stops at the pen chain next to Keshavrao's collar ring, far from Nagoji's mouth. A reader can easily take the challenge as Keshavrao's, and then his answer in 4.2 ("With you, I prefer...") stops making sense.
refuted.reason:
Refuted. I measured the tail on the 300 DPI render (page-04.png, original pixels).

- **Where the tail sits:** it leaves the top of the "You have seen the dungeon..." balloon at about (350, 955) and ends at about (402, 905).
- **Which way it points:** up and to the right, roughly 44 degrees above horizontal. Extended, that line passes through Nagoji's face at about x 630, y 685-755. His mouth is at about (630, 755).
- **Away from Keshavrao:** Keshavrao's visible cheek and jaw are up and to the LEFT of the tip, around (300-350, 730-820). His collar ring is about 100 px left of the tip, near (300, 920). The tail points away from both.
- **What the tip touches:** it stops by the pen chain Nagoji is holding, about 70 px from his own bandaged fist (around (470, 880)). That chain is Nagoji's, not Keshavrao's collar chain, so the reviewer's description of the tip position (about x350, y850, "beside Keshavrao's collar ring") does not match the art.

Putting the balloon over the foreground figure's back is the normal way to letter an over-the-shoulder shot. That part of the panel is empty space, and the tail is what tells the reader who is speaking. Here it leans clearly toward Nagoji.

The dialogue also makes the speaker clear. Page 3 ends with Keshavrao asking "And if there is no such thing?" Nagoji's two balloons answer him in order: the upper "Then we die here in the dark." reads first and its tail touches his chin. Keshavrao's close-up reply in 4.2 then follows naturally.

The only thing left is cosmetic. The tail is short (about 0.24 in at print) and stops about 0.9 in from Nagoji's mouth. Lengthening it toward his chin would be optional polish. It does not cause a misattribution that needs a redraw or re-letter.

refuted.description: Wrong speaker tail. Outside the costume lens, but plainly wrong. Nagoji's second line, 'You have seen the dungeon... Tell me which death you prefer', has its tail pointing at Keshavrao in the left foreground, so the line reads as Keshavrao's.
refuted.reason: The art does not support "wrong speaker tail." I zoomed page-04.png at full resolution (1838x2775) and traced the white tail pixels of the lower-left balloon "You have seen the dungeon... Tell me which death you prefer". The tail's base is at about x 320 to 360, y 958, on the balloon's top edge, and its tip is at about x 400, y 908. So it angles up and to the RIGHT, away from Keshavrao's head, which is up and to the left in the back-of-head foreground. When I drew that axis onward on a crop, the line ran through Nagoji's manacled fist and straight into his face, nose and mouth at about x 630, y 720 to 756. The tip is not on Keshavrao's collar: it sits in the dark wood gap between Keshavrao's collar ring (about x 300, y 910) and Nagoji's fist (about x 470, y 890), and it is slightly closer to Nagoji's fist. The reviewer's tip position (about x 400, y 870) is close to the real one, but the conclusion is wrong because the tail's direction plainly aims at Nagoji. Context agrees: the line is Nagoji's in the script (4.1), it is read after Nagoji's upper balloon, and Keshavrao answers it in 4.2. Keshavrao is also seen from behind, so a tail aimed away from his head does not read as his. The only real issue is polish. The tail is short and stops about 0.9 inch at 300 DPI from Nagoji's mouth, and the balloon body sits over Keshavrao's torso. Lengthening the tail toward Nagoji's mouth would remove any momentary doubt, but this is minor, not a major speaker error.

refuted.description: Nagoji's costume drifts across page 9. The 'torn ochre sleeveless tunic' turns into a voluminous ankle-length ochre robe with sleeves. In 9.3 both forearms are in ochre sleeves down to the bandages. In 9.4 the garment trails behind him like a cape to the deck, with a full sleeve on the far arm. In 9.5 ochre cloth covers his thigh and knee where the cream dhoti should be. Pages 8 (8.1, 8.3) and 10 (10.1, 10.3) show the correct hip-length sleeveless tunic, so the chapter's last pages flip between two costumes.
refuted.reason: The art doesn't show the costume flip that was reported, and the bible explains most of what it does show. Panel 9.4 is the panel the finding is anchored on. There, Nagoji's near arm is his right arm, because he faces right with his chest to camera. That arm is bare from the shoulder, so the tunic is sleeveless as the bible requires. Both thighs and the knee on the coil are clearly cream dhoti, so nothing reads as an "ankle-length robe". The ochre cloth on the far arm is his left forearm. The chapter 3 bible row says to keep his left arm covered so the brand stays hidden, and script 10.3 calls this "the ragged tunic flap still over his left forearm". So that is required, not drift. The ochre that seems to "trail to the deck" falls from his back and hip while he kneels low with his shin flat on the planks, and the storm is tearing at it. A thigh-length tunic does that in that pose. It is the same length as in 8.1 and 9.2, where the tunic also covers the upper thigh. In 9.5, the ochre over the knee is the tunic hem falling over a crouched knee, the same as in 9.2. It is a tight close-up and doesn't read as a second garment. The only leftover point is 9.3. There, both forearms, including the near right one, are wrapped in ochre down to the cuffs. But that is a sliver of the figure at the left frame edge. At print size it reads as wet torn tunic cloth hanging over his arms while he hauls, not as a different costume. At most it is optional polish, not a redraw. Face, collar, chains, bandages and color all stay consistent with pages 8 and 10.

refuted.description: The hatch ladder and the water are inconsistent within page 7. In 7.1 and 7.2 a narrow, steep plank ladder rises from shallow water, ankle-deep at Nagoji's feet. The script places 7.3 at the foot of that same ladder, yet it shows a broad staircase with side rails, and the prisoners stand chest-deep while the guard's body floats.
refuted.reason:
I zoomed into page 7 and the art does not support the claim.

1. **The "staircase" in 7.3 is the same ladder seen from above.** The panel looks down into the hold, as the script asks. Only the top five treads show, cut off at the bottom of the panel. They are flat plank treads between two side stringers, which is how the ladder is built in 7.1, where it is also a slanted ladder with flat treads rather than rungs. There are no separate handrails; the side boards are the stringers. The steps look wider only because they are right in front of the camera while the guard and prisoners are further away. At print size it reads as the top of the hatch ladder.

2. **The water depth is not inconsistent.** In 7.1, Nagoji is on the ladder and his lower foot just touches the surface. No floor is visible, so the panel does not show the water as ankle-deep. In 7.3, the prisoners sit against the bales with the water at about waist height, not chest height, and the guard floats face-down. The script calls for this:
   - 3.1: the water reaches the knee.
   - 4.5: it surges waist-deep.
   - 6.2: the foot of the ladder is thigh-deep.
   - 7.3: "the current rolls a still, face-down shape," which needs water deep enough to float a body.

   So 7.3 matches the script, and 7.1 shows nothing that contradicts it.

I'm not reporting this even as a minor issue, because the difference is only the change of viewpoint.

refuted.description: Caption reading order is inverted. The second caption ('It was the change in the way the ship moved.') sits flush on the left border at mid-height. The first caption ('The first warning was not the shout of a sailor or the crack of thunder.') sits top right. A left-to-right reader gets the payoff before the setup.
refuted.reason: I zoomed into page 1, panel 1.1 at full resolution and don't think the order is inverted. Standard lettering order reads the higher box first when two boxes don't share a line, which gives the script's order. The second caption also opens with "It was", which only makes sense as a reply to the first, so even a reader who glances left first would correct straight away. These centred tiers of varying width are therefore the house layout across the book, not a localized break on this page. Neither the script nor the bible asks for equal-width tiers on page 3. 2. **Tail: claim is wrong.** The right balloon's tail leaves its lower-left edge and goes down and left to end at Nagoji's temple, beside his eye. It never crosses Keshavrao's head, and the speaker is plainly Nagoji. There is no wrong-speaker problem.

Both 4.1 balloons are Nagoji's in the script, and the tails of both point to him, so Keshavrao's reply in 4.2 follows correctly. I refute this. The art does show Nagoji's left arm (viewer's right) bare from shoulder to wrist with no tunic flap. But the rule is satisfied another way. Script 1.1 and the CONTINUITY.md rows for chapters 1 to 3 say "covered OR turned from camera, so the brand stays hidden". The bible's chapter 4 row puts the brand on the INNER (ventral) left forearm, a hand's width above the wrist.

Zoomed crop of panel 7.4 (about x 780-1150, y 2100-2500 at full resolution): the left hand is palm-down on the hatch rim. The fingers curl over the near edge toward the camera, and the thumb sits on the medial side (viewer's left), which fits a pronated left hand. With the wrist bent back and the forearm rising almost vertically from the rim, the back (dorsal) side of the forearm faces the direction the fingers point, which is the camera. The muscle bulge below the elbow facing us is the outer forearm muscle. So we see the outer and back faces of the forearm. The inner face, where the brand would be, points away into the hatch.

The wrap and manacle also cover the wrist and the lowest part of the forearm. No mark is drawn, and none would be expected on the visible face, so nothing here contradicts the chapter 4 reveal. The script text for 7.4 itself asks only for "empty collar, manacles, bandaged hands" and does not call for the flap. Unlike 10.3 and 10.4, which do restate the flap, the arm here meets the "turned from camera" option. This is not a defect.
